blogs.title: Hiccups as a Medical Red Flag: Recognizing SIADH in Neuroinflammation
blogs.description: Severe hyponatremia in the context of encephalopathy or aseptic meningitis can manifest with bizarre and specific symptoms. In this rare case, persistent hiccups served as a critical clinical clue for SIADH secondary to acute neurological Behçet's disease. We discuss the classic signs of hyperventilation-induced SIADH complications, the importance of monitoring hiccups and urine output in febrile patients, and why recognizing these subtle signs can rapidize the start of appropriate fluid restriction therapy.

blogs.title: When MRI is Normal but the Nerves Are Hurting: Diagnosing Acute Neuro-Behçet's
blogs.description: A patient with acute neurological involvement in Behçet's disease often defies standard neuroimaging norms. Brain MRI is frequently normal in early acute neuro-BD, particularly in meningitis presentations without parenchymal lesions. This post emphasizes the critical role of cerebrospinal fluid analysis (lymphocytic pleocytosis, elevated protein) over imaging alone when ruling out malignancy in the differential diagnosis of fever and headache with negative infectious screens.

blogs.title: Colchicine Monotherapy in Acute Neuro-Behçet's: A Controversial Approach
blogs.description: Acute neuro-Behçet's typically requires aggressive steroid therapy, sometimes combined with IVIG or cyclophosphamide, while colchicine is often ineffective as monotherapy for CNS issues. This review examines our specific case where mucocutaneous symptoms, neurological signs, and SIADH resolved with colchicine alone. We analyze the mechanisms by which this anti-inflammatory agent works, the risks of withholding steroids, and when a milder regimen might be sufficient versus a standard immunosuppressive protocol.

blogs.title: Febrile Hyponatraemia: Navigating the Differential Between Infection and Autoimmune Inflammation
blogs.description: Before concluding a diagnosis of Behçet's in a febrile patient, clinicians must exhaustively rule out viral and bacterial etiologies for meningitis, myelitis, and paraneoplastic SIADH. We detail the systematic exclusion of HSV/VZV, bacterial meningitis, and sarcoidosis using CSF pleocytosis patterns, viral PCR, and CRP/sIL-2R analysis. This strategy helps avoid misdiagnosis and emphasizes the importance of a 'negative' infectious workup confirming the autoimmune hypothesis.

blogs.title: The Older Behçet's Patient: Managing Late-Onset Disease Versus Behçet's' Paranoia
blogs.description: Behçet's disease typically begins in late adolescence or early adulthood (20s-30s), presenting a diagnostic challenge when it manifests in a 60-year-old with a history of diabetes and no apparent genetic predisposition. We discuss the epidemiological rarity of Neuro-Behçet's in patients over 50, the clinical differences in presentation compared to young adults, and the implications for long-term monitoring and cardiovascular risk stratification in elderly patients with new-onset oriental vasculitis.
